_about: Plain words for the schedule, keyed by the spreadsheet's exact text. scripts/import-schedule.py swaps them in. If the spreadsheet changes, the script lists any text with no plain version here.

focus.Enforcement and handoffs: Must-do checks and passing to a person
focus.MCP and tool failures: MCP and when tools go wrong

Nothing to do. Rest is part of the plan.
start.Open an unseen mock. Set 120 minutes. Cl: New practice test: 2 hours, no notes, no AI.
start.Open one unresolved error. Change one co: Change one mistake. Guess the new answer.
start.Open the exam outline. Rate the first fi: Mark how well you know 5 exam topics.
start.Open the existing exercise; run one know: Run one thing in your project that works.
start.Open the named objective and your last r: Read your last note. Try one question first.
start.Open the reserved mock or the two select: Alerts off. Start your saved test or 2 weakest topics.
start.Open this week’s objective IDs. Write: “: Write: 'By Saturday I can…'. Try the first question.
start.Read your pre-break restart note. Attemp: Read your pre-break note. Try one easy example.

evidence.One brief MD entry: decision attempted;: Write a short note. Say what you tried, what is still hard and what to do next.
After the exam, write down how it went.

minimum.10 minutes: attempt one decision, check: Only 10 minutes? Try one question. Check it. Write down the next small step. Do not tick the topic as done.
minimum.25 minutes: run one case, predict one ch: Only 25 minutes? Run one example. Guess what happens if you change one thing. Leave a 'start here next time' note. Move the rest to an extra hour.
minimum.If childcare removes the day, move prote: If childcare takes the day, move your day off if you can. Do not squeeze a full practice test into bits.
minimum.Reschedule the full mock into a protecte: Move the full practice test to a time nobody can take. A test done in bits does not count as a timed test.

recall.First 10 minutes: recall one decision fr: First 10 minutes: from memory, say one thing you worked out last time.
recall.First 10 minutes: recall your most recen: First 10 minutes: think of the last thing you got wrong. If there is nothing, try one starter question.
recall.No retrieval before the mock. Review ans: No warm-up before the test. Check your answers after.
recall.No warm-up answers before the mock. Revi: No warm-up before the test. After, look at the ones you got wrong or guessed.

how.Attempt three fresh decisions for this t: Before you read, try 3 new questions on this topic. Pick the 2 you found hardest. Write one thing you will be able to show by Saturday. If you got all 3 right and can say why, read less and fix an older weak spot instead.
how.Use only the subsection needed for Monda: Only read the part you need for Monday's weak spot. Stop reading after 20 minutes. Then explain it out loud with no help.
how.Answer before asking Claude; explain the: Answer first, then ask Claude. Say why the next best answer is wrong.
how.Optional repair slot. If tired or core w: This hour is a choice. If you are tired, or you are up to date, skip it.
how.Compress: update at most five short deci: Tidy your notes: change no more than 5 short rules. Add one real example or a quick drawing to a hard rule.
how.Use three 45-minute work blocks with two: Work in three 45-minute blocks, with two 15-minute breaks and 15 minutes to finish. Look at one example that works. Change one thing. Then try a new case.

task.Set a single study workspace and choose: Pick one place to study. Pick one thing you always do to start, like making a tea. Answer first, then ask Claude. Read the exam guide. For each of the 30 topics, mark it: new to me, I know it a bit, or I can do it. Check you are allowed to take the exam.
task.Attempt the 12 official sample questions: Try the 12 sample questions from the exam makers. Hide the answers. If you guess, write it down as a gap. 12 questions is too few to tell if you are ready.
task.Review missed sample questions. Select t: Look at the sample questions you got wrong. Pick 3 things to learn first. Write down what you can already do.
task.Organise the official guide, companion g: Sort your things: the exam guide, the helper guide and your list of mistakes. Look at one thing you have built before. Find what goes in, which tools it uses, what comes out and where it breaks. Check once that your study things are up to date.
task.Recall baseline gaps. Learn JSON objects: Think back to the gaps you found. Learn JSON: objects, lists, words (strings), numbers and null (empty). Write notes on a short example.
task.Read a tool schema. Identify required fi: Read a tool schema (the form that says what a tool needs). Find what it must have, what it may have, which values are allowed and what is missing.
task.Trace a request, tool call, tool result: Follow one message all the way: you ask, Claude asks for a tool, the tool answers, Claude replies. Say who runs the tool. (Your code does, not Claude.)
task.Inspect a short Python or JavaScript exa: Look at a short bit of Python or JavaScript with Claude. Say what it does, step by step, before you ask for help.
task.Without notes, redraw the request/result: With no notes, draw the steps again: ask, tool, answer, reply. Pick one tech basics gap that is left.
task.Use Claude Code to create a tiny fake-or: Use Claude Code to make a tiny pretend shop order lookup. Guess what goes in and what comes out. Run it. Change one thing and look at what happens. No screens to build and nothing to put online.
task.Break the loop into request, stop reason: Break the loop into 4 parts: the ask, the reason Claude stopped, running the tool, and sending the result back. Guess the next step for each part.
task.Study tool_use versus end_turn and how t: Learn tool_use and end_turn. tool_use means Claude wants a tool. end_turn means Claude is finished. Learn how a tool's answer goes back into the chat.
task.Answer six fresh loop scenarios. Explain: Answer 6 new questions about the loop. Say why words alone do not mean Claude is finished.
task.Inspect multiple tool calls and missing: Look at more than one tool call at once, and at tool answers that are missing. Guess what will go wrong.
task.Recall JSON basics and loop decisions. W: Think back to JSON and the loop. Write 5 short rules.
task.Extend the fake-order agent into a compl: Make the shop agent into a full loop. Test 3 things: it finishes normally, it uses a tool, and a tool gives a strange answer. Say why stopping properly is better than a hard limit on turns.
task.Identify when instructions are sufficien: Work out when telling Claude is enough, and when a step must be checked by code because it must always happen.
task.Study tool interception and result-norma: Learn about hooks: code that steps in before a tool runs, or tidies a tool's answer after. Say how a check before is different from a check after.
task.Practise verification-before-refund, pol: Practise 3 cases: check who someone is before a refund, cases where the rules allow an exception, and when someone asks for a person.
task.Write a useful handoff containing verifi: Write a good handover to a person. Say who the customer is (checked), the problem, what was tried and what to do next.
task.Recall loop decisions. Distinguish manda: Think back to the loop. In 3 new cases, tell apart a check that must happen from a helpful hint.
task.Add verification and a refund-limit chec: Add 2 checks to the support practice: check who someone is, and a refund limit. Try to get round them. Test the answer tidying. Make a handover to a person.
task.Compare two overlapping tools. Identify: Compare 2 tools that do nearly the same thing. Find where the description of what each does, what it takes, or where it stops is unclear.
task.Rewrite the descriptions with examples a: Rewrite the tool descriptions with examples and clear limits. Say when one big tool should be split into smaller ones.
task.Answer fresh tool-routing scenarios and: Answer new questions about which tool Claude should pick. Compare the 3 choices in the exam guide: auto, any and forced.
task.Assign tools to roles. Justify limited a: Give each role only the tools it needs. Say why fewer tools is safer. Do not learn a magic number of tools.
task.Recall enforcement and schemas. Review f: Think back to must-happen checks and schemas. Look at 5 unclear requests before you see the suggested answers.
task.Test similar lookup tools against ten re: Test tools that look alike with 10 requests. Make the descriptions better. Run the ones that failed again. Say if each fix solved the real problem.
task.Separate tools from resources. Explain w: Tell tools apart from resources. Say what an MCP server gives to an agent. (MCP is a standard way to plug tools into Claude.)
task.Inspect project versus personal MCP conf: Look at MCP settings for a whole project and for just you. Look at how settings point to secret values without writing them in.
task.Classify timeout, invalid input, policy: Sort these into groups: too slow (timeout), bad input, blocked by a rule, not allowed, and worked but found nothing.
task.Design error fields that communicate cat: Design an error message that says: what kind of error, whether to try again, why it happened, and any part that did work.
task.Recall tool boundaries. Predict the appr: Think back to what each tool should do. Guess the right fix for 5 new kinds of failure.
task.Connect one suitable MCP example or use: Connect one simple MCP example, or use a pretend one on your computer. Make things fail on purpose. Check it tries again, explains, or hands over when it should. Do not set up servers online.
task.Map personal, project and directory inst: Map where instructions can live: just for you, for the project, or for one folder. Work out why a teammate might not get a rule.
task.Study modular imports and path-scoped ru: Learn how instruction files can pull in other files, and how a rule can apply only to some folders. Match rules to the right files.
task.Compare persistent instructions with reu: Compare instructions that are always on with skills and commands you call when needed. Say where each applies and what each can see.
task.Inspect skill frontmatter: isolated cont: Look at the top of a skill file. Find: its own separate memory, which tools it may use, and hints for what to type.
task.Recall MCP scope. Answer fresh instructi: Think back to MCP settings. Answer new questions about where an instruction should live and which rule applies.
task.Configure the practice repository with p: Set up the practice project with project instructions, 2 folder rules and 1 small skill. Show each one working. Explain the setup with no notes.
task.Choose content search, filename search,: For a set of jobs, choose the right way to look: search inside files, search for file names, read a file, or edit it.
task.Compare plan mode with direct execution: Compare plan mode (Claude plans first) with just doing it. Try it on a small fix and on a change to many files.
task.Practise concrete input/output examples,: Practise 3 ways to help Claude: give clear examples of what goes in and what comes out, write tests first, and ask questions when unsure.
task.Trace a small codebase using targeted se: Find your way round a small code project using searches. Do not read every file at once.
task.Recall instruction scope. Explain when i: Think back to where instructions live. Say when problems that affect each other should be fixed together.
task.Use the repository for a small fix and a: Use the project for a small fix and a bigger planned change. Give Claude the failing tests so it can improve. Check the final changes yourself.
task.Recall the last four weeks without notes: From memory, with no notes, think back over the last 4 weeks. Pick the 2 things you are weakest at.
task.Repair the first weakness using a target: Fix the first weak spot. Use one part of the guide and one new example.
task.Complete a 30-minute mixed question set;: Do 30 minutes of mixed questions. Then spend 30 minutes looking at what you got wrong.
task.Flexible catch-up: finish one incomplete: Catch-up time: finish one practice task you did not finish, or rest if you are up to date.
task.Create concise reference sheets for arch: Make short notes sheets for 3 areas: how it all fits together, tools, and Claude Code. Write down how you will start again in January.
task.Demonstrate the support agent and config: Show the support agent and the set-up project working. Explain 3 failures you cause on purpose, with no help. Use any time left only for main work you have not done.
task.Christmas break. No required study or ca: Christmas break. No study and no catch-up.
task.Return from Christmas: recall key decisi: Back from Christmas. Think back to the key ideas. Then find the unclear words in a review prompt.
task.Replace vague criteria with report/ignor: Swap unclear words for clear rules: what to report, what to ignore, and examples of how serious each thing is.
task.Create a few examples for ambiguous extr: Write a few examples for hard cases where Claude pulls facts out of text. Say how the examples help with new cases.
task.Design required, nullable and enum field: Design fields that must be filled, fields that can be empty (nullable) and fields with a fixed list of choices (enum). See that the right shape does not mean the facts are right.
task.Answer mixed prompt/schema questions and: Answer mixed questions on prompts and schemas. Look again at one mistake from before Christmas.
task.Build a small extraction exercise with f: Make a small practice that pulls facts out of pretend invoices. Test missing details, different layouts and facts that do not agree. Compare the results before and after you change the prompt or schema.
task.Diagnose syntax, schema and semantic err: Spot 3 kinds of error: broken format (syntax), wrong shape (schema) and wrong meaning. Find missing facts that trying again cannot fix.
task.Design a retry containing the original d: Design a retry that sends back the first document, the wrong answer and the exact error.
task.Choose batch or synchronous processing f: Choose a batch (many jobs at once, results later) or a normal request (answer now). Do it for checks that must finish first and for reports that can wait overnight.
task.Match results using custom_id and calcul: Match each result to its job using custom_id. Work out when results will be ready from the batch time limit.
task.Recall nullable fields. Practise selecti: Think back to fields that can be empty. Practise trying again only for the jobs that failed, and finding which ones failed.
task.Add semantic checks and a bounded correc: Add meaning checks to the fact pulling, and a fix-up loop with a limit. Pretend to run a batch where some jobs fail. Try again only those. Write down what still needs a person to check.
task.Explain non-interactive execution and st: Explain how Claude can run with nobody typing, and give its findings in a fixed shape, for an automatic code review.
task.Inspect a small CI example; identify pro: Look at a small automatic check set-up (CI). Find the project instructions and the tests it gives Claude to read.
task.Compare same-session self-review with an: Compare Claude checking its own work in the same chat with a separate reviewer that starts fresh.
task.Split a large review into local passes a: Split a big review into small checks of each file, then one check of how the files work together.
task.Practise avoiding duplicate comments and: Practise not repeating the same comments or the same tests when a review runs again.
task.Run a small non-interactive review local: Run a small review on your computer with nobody typing. Compare a narrow check with a wide one. Run it again after a fix, giving it the earlier findings. No need to set it up for real.
task.Decompose a research question into compl: Break a research question into parts that fit together. Check that nothing is missing.
task.Study coordinator responsibilities, expl: Learn what the boss agent does, how it hands work over clearly, and how each helper gets only the tools it needs.
task.Explain parallel versus sequential deleg: Say when helpers should work at the same time or one after another. Say why helpers must be given the facts they need. (They cannot see the main chat.)
task.Design structured results with claim, so: Design a results shape with: the claim, where it came from, the proof and the date.
task.Recall tool failures. Predict how a coor: Think back to tool failures. Guess how the boss agent should react when the joined-up answer has gaps.
task.Build a coordinator with two small resea: Build a boss agent with 2 small research helpers. Test missing facts, helpers doing the same job, and parts left out. Send one helper back to fill one gap. Explain the handovers.
task.Identify exact facts that must survive s: Find the exact facts that must not be lost when a chat is summed up. Cut tool output that does not matter.
task.Choose resume, fresh summary or a separa: When files or ideas change, choose: carry on, start fresh with a summary, or start a separate path.
task.Design persistent findings and a recover: Design notes that last, and a list that lets research pick up again after it stops.
task.Preserve conflicting claims with attribu: When sources disagree, keep both claims, with who said it and when. Do not quietly pick one.
task.Recall independent review. Practise stru: Think back to the separate reviewer. Practise failure reports that say what was tried and what did work.
task.Interrupt the research exercise, restore: Stop the research practice part way. Bring it back. Pretend one source is down. Keep the case facts, sources, dates and a clear list of what is missing.
task.Distinguish policy gaps, inability to pr: Tell apart 3 reasons to pass to a person: no rule covers it, Claude is stuck, or the customer asks. A customer being upset is not enough on its own.
task.Understand field-level confidence calibr: Learn confidence scores for each field, checked against examples where the right answer is known.
task.Break extraction accuracy down by docume: Break down how often fact pulling is right, by kind of document and by field. Find weak spots that the overall score hides.
task.Design a small stratified review sample,: Design a small check by a person that picks some of each kind, including some answers Claude was sure about.
task.Check all 30 objectives. Flag unresolved: Check all 30 topics. Mark the ones still not sorted. Check once that the exam and study details are up to date.
task.Test the extraction review process. Comp: Test how a person checks the fact pulling. Do a short mixed timed set and look at your guesses. Write a 'start here next time' note for after the holiday. Save new full practice tests for later.
task.One-week holiday. No required study. Res: One week of holiday. No study. Start again on 22 February.
task.After holiday: recall core decisions and: After the holiday: think back to the main ideas and read your 'start here next time' note. Pick the topics you are likely weak at.
task.Practise short mixed scenarios without a: Practise short mixed questions with no help. Say why the most tempting wrong answer is wrong.
task.Confirm the next day is protected prepar: Check that tomorrow is your protected day off work. Get a new 60-question practice test ready.
task.PREPARATION DAY 1: sit a fresh 120-minut: STUDY DAY 1: do a new 2-hour practice test. Take a proper break. Look at what you got wrong or guessed. Then fix your 2 biggest gaps. 5 hours in all.
task.Review the mock error log. Separate know: Look at the mistakes from the practice test. Sort them: did not know it, read it wrong, or ran out of time.
task.Optional buffer only: finish mock correc: Spare time only: finish fixing test mistakes, or a practice task you missed. No new full test. Your study day takes the place of Saturday's long session.
task.Select the two weakest domains using the: Use the practice test to pick your 2 weakest areas. Write down the exact things to fix.
task.Repair the first domain with a small fai: Fix the first weak area with a small example of it going wrong and 6 new questions.
task.Repair the second domain; explain why te: Fix the second weak area. Say why the tempting wrong answers are wrong.
task.Review all domains briefly, including mu: Look quickly at all areas. Include how questions with more than one right answer work.
task.Light closed-book recall. Prepare a fres: Think back with no notes, just a little. Get a new practice test ready. Do not reuse questions you remember.
task.Sit mock 2 for 120 minutes. Break, then: Do practice test 2 for 2 hours. Take a break. Then spend 1 hour on what you got wrong or guessed. Compare with test 1.
task.Compare mock results and select remainin: Compare your test results. Pick the mistakes you keep making. Check your exam booking.
task.Work through fresh scenarios for the mos: Work through new questions on the idea you keep getting wrong.
task.Practise a second weak area and explain: Practise a second weak area. Explain the set-up or the steps it goes through.
task.Recall decisions from earlier weeks; che: Think back to earlier weeks. Check that for every topic you have shown you can do it on your own.
task.Short mixed review; prepare the next day: A short mixed look back. Get tomorrow's new practice test ready, but do not read its answers.
task.Sit mock 3 for 120 minutes, then review: Do practice test 3 for 2 hours. Take a break, then look at your answers. The aim is 85% or more on 2 new tests, with no big weak area that keeps coming back. This is a study aim, not the real pass mark.
task.Readiness decision: review fresh mocks,: Decide if you are ready. Look at your new test scores, your timing and how well you explained. If big gaps are left, move the exam before the booking deadline.
task.PREPARATION DAY 2: repair remaining weak: STUDY DAY 2: fix the weak spots that are left with small tasks and new questions. Teach all 5 areas out loud. 5 hours with breaks. Nothing new.
task.Review only mistakes from the preparatio: Look only at the mistakes from your study day. Write short, fixed rules.
task.Check ID, booking instructions, travel o: Check your ID, your booking details, how you will get there or what your computer needs, and your childcare.
task.Review the five reference sheets without: Read your 5 notes sheets. Do not add to them. Stop after 1 hour.
task.Optional one-hour buffer only. Finish a: Spare hour only, if you want it. Finish one small thing or rest. Your study day takes the place of Saturday's long session.
task.Spend 45 minutes recalling the most impo: Spend 45 minutes thinking back to the most important ideas. Then stop.
task.Spend 45 minutes on a small fresh mixed: Spend 45 minutes on a few new mixed questions. Check them calmly. No full test.
task.Spend 30 minutes reviewing recurring mis: Spend 30 minutes on the mistakes you keep making, and check your exam plans.
task.No studying. Prepare ID and arrangements: No study. Get your ID and plans ready. Rest, and sort out childcare.
task.EXAM DAY: assumed Friday 26 March. Follo: EXAM DAY. It is planned for Friday 26 March. Follow your booking and check-in steps. No study today.
